proposed.title: Keep experimental halving estimators out of wildcard exports
answers: Why does from sklearn.model_selection import * raise ImportError?
Can experimental halving search estimators be added to __all__?
How should model_selection expose HalvingGridSearchCV and HalvingRandomSearchCV?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Star-importing sklearn.model_selection fails with an ImportError about enabling halving search.
Root cause: sklearn/model_selection/__init__.py:__all__ listed HalvingGridSearchCV and HalvingRandomSearchCV, whose access is rejected by sklearn/model_selection/__init__.py:__getattr__ until enable_halving_search_cv is imported.
Fix pattern: Exclude gated estimators from __all__; retain their TYPE_CHECKING imports with # noqa: F401 for static visibility.
Constraints: Applies while these estimators are experimental. Preserve the guidance error on explicit access before opt-in and their importability after opt-in; revisit the type-checking workaround when they cease to be experimental.
proposed.applies: Changes to model_selection exports and experimental halving-search exposure.

proposed.title: Validate public wildcard imports in a fresh interpreter
answers: Why can import consistency tests miss a broken wildcard import?
How do we test public imports without accidentally enabling experimental estimators?
Where is the regression check for star-importing public sklearn modules?
proposed.body:
sklearn/tests/test_common.py:test_wildcard_import_for_public_modules validates wildcard imports in a fresh interpreter because test_common itself enables halving search, which can hide import failures in the test process.
It enumerates top-level modules with pkgutil.iter_modules, excluding underscore-prefixed names, tests and conftest, and executes their wildcard imports through assert_run_python_script_without_output.
The subprocess also asserts that no sklearn.experimental.* modules entered sys.modules: public wildcard imports must not implicitly activate experimental features.
The test is marked xfail on _IS_WASM because that environment cannot start a subprocess.
proposed.applies: Regression coverage for public module exports and experimental import side effects.

proposed.title: Allow 64-bit sparse indices in spectral ARPACK validation
answers: Why does SpectralEmbedding fail with a 64-bit sparse indices ValueError under sparray?
SpectralClustering fails when sparse_interface="sparray" is enabled.
How should the spectral ARPACK path validate sparse Laplacians?
proposed.body:
Symptom: SpectralEmbedding and SpectralClustering raise a ValueError about 64-bit sparse indices under config_context(sparse_interface="sparray") with eigen_solver="arpack".
Root cause: sklearn/manifold/_spectral_embedding.py:_spectral_embedding rejected large sparse indices during Laplacian validation, although eigsh supports them; sparse arrays do not downcast indices based on content.
Fix pattern: Keep CSR validation without accept_large_sparse=False for this eigsh path. Verify backend equivalence up to eigenvector sign, as in sklearn/manifold/tests/test_spectral_embedding.py:test_spectral_embedding_sparse_interface_sparray.
Constraints: Applies to the shared spectral ARPACK path, including its shift-invert eigsh call; do not generalize removal of index-width restrictions to consumers that require 32-bit index buffers.
proposed.applies: Spectral embedding and clustering using the shared ARPACK solver path with sparse Laplacians.

proposed.title: Stop stalled Newton line searches without marking them converged
answers: Why does the Newton solver line search emit a divide-by-zero warning?
How should backtracking handle an unchanged step length?
Should hitting the minimum line-search step count as convergence?
proposed.body:
Symptom: The Newton solver emits a divide-by-zero warning during a failing line search.
Root cause: sklearn/linear_model/_glm/_newton_solver.py:NewtonSolver can reduce alpha to the same value as alpha_old, including at min_step_length; another iteration then divides by a zero denominator.
Fix pattern: Exit backtracking when the reduced step length is unchanged. Track convergence explicitly at each acceptance branch so an unsuccessful early exit still emits the line-search failure warning.
Constraints: Applies when successive step lengths are identical. Stopping a stalled search avoids the arithmetic warning but does not make the search converge; only a successful acceptance check marks convergence.
proposed.applies: NewtonSolver backtracking step reduction, acceptance checks, and line-search failure reporting.

proposed.title: Preserved pandas input needs explicit finite-value validation in selectors
answers: Why does SelectKBest accept infinity with pandas output?
How should feature selectors validate DataFrames with set_output(transform="pandas")?
Does VarianceThreshold allow infinity as well as NaN during transform?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Feature selectors accept infinity or NaN during transform with pandas output even when the selector disallows NaN.
Root cause: sklearn/feature_selection/_base.py:SelectorMixin.transform uses skip_check_array=preserve_X, bypassing the array-level finite-value check when preserving the DataFrame.
Fix pattern: When preserving input bypasses array validation, explicitly call assert_all_finite(X, input_name="X") before _transform for selectors whose input_tags.allow_nan is false.
Constraints: The guard rejects both infinity and NaN only when allow_nan is false. When true, both pass through, matching the NumPy path; sklearn/feature_selection/tests/test_variance_threshold.py:test_transform_dataframe_allow_nan explicitly tests this exception.
proposed.applies: Feature selectors using SelectorMixin.transform with preserved pandas input and pandas output.

proposed.title: Use NaN-filtered sorted weights when averaging weighted percentiles
answers: Why does the maximum weighted percentile return NaN despite ignoring missing values?
How should _weighted_percentile handle NaNs with average=True?
Which weights should weighted-percentile averaging use to detect zero-weight samples?
proposed.body:
Symptom: The 100th weighted percentile can return NaN when missing values should be ignored and average=True.
Root cause: sklearn/utils/stats.py:_weighted_percentile checked the next sample's original weight, which did not reflect the zero weight assigned to NaNs in sorted_weights.
Fix pattern: Check zero-weight eligibility using sorted_weights and the corresponding sorted indices so averaging respects the effective weights used to ignore NaNs.
Constraints: This failure occurs with average=True at percentile_rank=100 because sorted NaNs are last; sklearn/utils/tests/test_stats.py:test_weighted_percentile_nan_filtered checks equivalence to removing NaNs for ranks 0, 30, and 100, both averaging modes, and one- or two-dimensional weights.
proposed.applies: The private _weighted_percentile helper's NaN filtering and zero-weight handling during averaging.

proposed.title: Cache callback hook signatures without retaining callback instances
answers: Why do scoring monitor resources remain alive after fitting and discarding the callback?
How should callback hook signatures be cached?
Why does the signature cache grow with each callback instance?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Callback objects and their resources remain alive after they are no longer used, and the signature cache grows with callback instances.
Root cause: sklearn/callback/_callback_context.py:CallbackContext cached bound hooks, which hold strong references to their callback instances.
Fix pattern: Inspect and cache getattr(hook, "__func__", hook), sharing the signature of the underlying function; invoke the original hook to preserve method binding.
Constraints: Applies to callback hook signature caching. Preserve the fallback for hooks without __func__; unbinding is for signature inspection, not hook invocation.
proposed.applies: Callback hook signature caching and dispatch in CallbackContext.

proposed.title: Exercise fitting before checking ScoringMonitor garbage collection
answers: How do I test that a scoring monitor releases its listener?
Why can a callback cleanup test miss a signature-cache leak?
How do I reproduce scoring monitor resources surviving callback deletion?
proposed.body:
ScoringMonitor cleanup tests must exercise fitting before checking collection, because fitting triggers callback signature caching.
In sklearn/callback/tests/test_scoring_monitor.py:test_scoring_monitor_listener_closed_on_gc, fit a temporary estimator with the callback, delete the callback, and call gc.collect().
Verify that the listener address disappears from both _listeners and _message_consumers; checking only construction and deletion misses retention introduced during fitting.
proposed.applies: Regression tests for ScoringMonitor listener cleanup after callback use.

proposed.title: Normalize NumPy-backed containers before cross-namespace array transfer
answers: Why do classification metrics fail with pandas labels and array API predictions?
How should move_to handle pandas Series or Python lists?
Where should array-like inputs become NumPy arrays before DLPack transfer?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Classification metrics reject pandas labels when array API dispatch is enabled and predictions use another namespace or device.
Root cause: sklearn/utils/_array_api.py:move_to passed NumPy-namespace containers into transfer logic without first converting them to NumPy ndarrays.
Fix pattern: Normalize these containers with numpy.asarray before cross-namespace transfer; preserve the subsequent NumPy-to-PyTorch negative-stride contiguity guard, which prevents a process abort during DLPack import.
Constraints: Normalize only when the source namespace is NumPy, the destination namespace is non-NumPy, and the input is not already a numpy.ndarray. Preserve the existing same-namespace, same-device fast path.
proposed.applies: Array-like inputs transferred through move_to from the NumPy namespace to another array API namespace, including pandas classification labels.

proposed.title: Freeze elapsed-time displays for finished progress tasks
answers: Why do completed progress bars keep counting time in meta-estimators?
How should ProgressBar timers behave with max_propagation_depth > 0?
Which duration should render use for a finished progress task?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Full progress bars in meta-estimators keep counting time while subsequent bars fill when max_propagation_depth > 0.
Root cause: sklearn/callback/_progressbar.py:render used task.elapsed for finished tasks, so the displayed duration continued increasing.
Fix pattern: Use task.finished_time to display the fixed completion duration when elapsed_when_finished and task.finished are both true.
Constraints: Apply this to finished-task elapsed displays; the other branch continues to use task.time_remaining.
proposed.applies: ProgressBar task-time rendering, including completed tasks displayed during propagated meta-estimator progress.

proposed.title: Normalize LDA targets to X through integer encoding
answers: LDA fit fails when X and y use different devices
Can LinearDiscriminantAnalysis accept string labels with array API features?
How should LDA handle targets from another array namespace?
proposed.body:
Symptom: LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.fit raises when labels use a different namespace or device from the features, including string labels.
Root cause: sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.fit performed X-namespace target operations without first normalizing y; raw strings cannot be represented by array API namespaces.
Fix pattern: Derive classes_ from the original y, encode y against those classes, then move the integer codes to X's namespace and device before estimating priors and invoking solvers.
Constraints: This normalization applies to computational target codes; it does not require transferring original labels. Preserve the original-label classes_ mapping, and do not attempt to transfer raw string labels into an array API namespace.
proposed.applies: Target preparation in LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.fit, especially mixed namespace/device inputs and string labels.

proposed.title: LDA helpers share one positional class encoding
answers: What targets do LDA class statistics helpers accept?
How do LDA means and covariances stay aligned with classes and priors?
How can LDA avoid repeatedly computing unique labels?
proposed.body:
Invariant: Computational targets are integer codes indexing classes_; class means, covariance weights, and SVD groups must use that same positional mapping.
Mechanism: sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:LinearDiscriminantAnalysis.fit encodes once; the solvers pass classes_.shape[0] as n_classes to _class_means and _class_cov.
Enforcement: sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:_class_means, sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:_class_cov, and sklearn/discriminant_analysis.py:LinearDiscriminantAnalysis._solve_svd group samples by integer positions.
Constraints: Helper callers must supply encoded targets and the matching class count. Passing arbitrary raw labels breaks positional grouping; helpers should not recompute unique labels from the target.
proposed.applies: Changes to LDA solver plumbing or shared class-statistics helpers in discriminant_analysis.py.

answers: Why does cross-validation pass a Narwhals dataframe to my estimator?

Root cause: sklearn/utils/validation.py:_make_indexable converted dataframe inputs with nw.from_native instead of returning them unchanged.

proposed.title: Move GLM targets and weights before dtype-coupled validation
answers: Why does PoissonRegressor fail when targets or sample weights use a different array backend?
Can PoissonRegressor fit or score with CPU targets and GPU features?
Where should mixed namespace inputs be converted before GLM validation?
proposed.body:
Symptom: PoissonRegressor fit or score raises a dtype TypeError when y or sample_weight uses a different array API namespace or device than X.
Root cause: sklearn/linear_model/_glm/glm.py:_GeneralizedLinearRegressor.fit and _GeneralizedLinearRegressor.score validated auxiliary inputs against X-derived dtypes before moving them, allowing a foreign backend dtype to reach validation.

Constraints: This ordering applies to GLM validation coupled to X.dtype in fit or raw_prediction.dtype in score. The move is a no-op for same-namespace inputs and does not replace dtype or sample-weight validation.
proposed.applies: Array API target and sample-weight handling in _GeneralizedLinearRegressor.fit and .score, including PoissonRegressor.

proposed.title: Transform routed validation data alongside training data by default
answers: Why does my pipeline transform training data but leave the validation set unchanged?
How does Pipeline preprocess X_val?
What should transform_input default to?
proposed.body:
Symptom: The validation set reaches an estimator without the preprocessing applied to the training data.
Root cause: sklearn/pipeline.py:Pipeline.__init__ and sklearn/pipeline.py:make_pipeline previously defaulted transform_input to None, requiring callers to opt into transforming X_val.
Fix pattern: Keep both constructors defaulting to ("X_val",); sklearn/pipeline.py:Pipeline._parameter_constraints accepts tuple, list, and None to support this default and explicit overrides.
Constraints: Validation metadata transformation requires metadata routing and follows pipeline steps up to the consuming step. Explicit transform_input overrides determine which metadata is transformed.
proposed.applies: Pipeline and make_pipeline defaults, parameter validation, and validation-set preprocessing through metadata routing.

proposed.title: Preserve ordinary fitting when metadata routing is disabled
answers: Why can Pipeline fit with its default transform_input when routing is disabled?
Why does transform_input=["X_val"] raise but the default tuple does not?
Why does passing X_val to fit fail without metadata routing?
proposed.body:
Invariant: With metadata routing disabled, the default transform_input=("X_val",) must allow ordinary fitting without validation metadata.
Enforcement: sklearn/pipeline.py:Pipeline.fit rejects transform_input only when it is truthy and differs from ("X_val",); None and empty lists or tuples also bypass this guard.
Boundary: The exemption compares the actual value, so ["X_val"] still triggers the transform_input guard. Passing X_val to fit with the default instead produces the usual "Pipeline.fit does not accept" error.
Regression coverage: sklearn/tests/test_pipeline.py:test_transform_input_no_slep6 checks custom-input rejection, ordinary default fitting, and rejection of supplied X_val; removing the default exemption would break ordinary fitting with routing disabled.
proposed.applies: Pipeline.fit compatibility and error handling when metadata routing is disabled.

proposed.title: Route bagging prediction metadata to the method actually invoked
answers: Why is metadata routed incorrectly during BaggingClassifier.predict_proba?
How should bagging route metadata when a base estimator lacks predict_proba?
Which parameters belong to predict_proba versus the voting fallback?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Metadata supplied to BaggingClassifier.predict_proba is routed incorrectly to the underlying estimator's prediction method.

Fix pattern: When selecting the consuming method dynamically, pass the parameters routed for that method: predict_proba_params to predict_proba, and predict_params to predict.
Constraints: In this helper, estimators exposing predict_proba use that method; estimators without it use predict for voting. Choose metadata by the method actually invoked, not solely by the public ensemble method.

proposed.title: Inspect native pandas data when validating Narwhals DataFrames
answers: Why does check_array fail on a Narwhals DataFrame?
How should check_array inspect pandas-backed Narwhals input?
How should sparse pandas columns behave when wrapped in Narwhals?
proposed.body:
Symptom: check_array errors when input is already a Narwhals DataFrame backed by pandas.
Root cause: sklearn/utils/validation.py:check_array accessed pandas-specific dtype and sparse interfaces on the input, which may be a Narwhals wrapper.
Fix pattern: Obtain the native pandas DataFrame with array_df.to_native(); use it for dtype inspection, sparse-column detection, and fully sparse conversion through sparse.to_coo().
Constraints: This pattern applies to pandas-backed DataFrames. Fully sparse DataFrames must enter sparse validation and honor accept_sparse; DataFrames with only some sparse columns warn that conversion will produce a dense NumPy array. Do not generalize pandas-specific inspection to other backends.
proposed.applies: check_array handling of native pandas DataFrames and pandas-backed Narwhals DataFrames, especially sparse columns.

Fully sparse DataFrames must enter sparse validation and honor accept_sparse; DataFrames with only some sparse columns warn that conversion will produce a dense NumPy array. Do not generalize pandas-specific inspection to other backends.

proposed.title: Normalize NMF factor layouts at the coordinate-descent boundary
answers: Why does NMF fit_transform fail with 'ndarray is not C-contiguous'?
How should NMF handle changes in SciPy SVD output ordering?
What array layouts does the NMF coordinate-descent solver require?
proposed.body:
Symptom: NMF fit_transform raises ValueError: ndarray is not C-contiguous with SciPy development versions.
Root cause: sklearn/decomposition/_nmf.py:_fit_coordinate_descent did not normalize W's memory layout, allowing changes in SciPy SVD output ordering to reach the coordinate-descent kernel.
Fix pattern: At sklearn/decomposition/_nmf.py:_fit_coordinate_descent, normalize W and H.T with np.ascontiguousarray before updates, and convert CSC input X to CSR.
Constraints: Enforce the factor layout requirement at the coordinate-descent boundary regardless of initialization; do not rely on upstream SVD output ordering. This requirement is specific to coordinate descent and does not establish a layout requirement for the multiplicative-update solver.
proposed.applies: NMF coordinate-descent initialization and solver input preparation.
